requirement:
# DEF-FLISR-7 — restoration back-fed a de-energised section

During drill 14 the restoration plan closed a tie switch that re-energised the faulted section.
Expected: the faulted section stays isolated. Observed: `plan_restoration` returned a close action
on the tie adjacent to the faulted section. Reproduce with the drill-14 savecase in `backend/tests/data`.

artifacts.explore.hypothesis: build_plan (backend/app/flisr.py) never treats a tie switch as a boundary of the faulted section: _isolation_switches skips ties (flisr.py:42) and the restoration loop (flisr.py:91-122, via _nodes_restored_by flisr.py:136-151) never removes the faulted section's nodes from a tie's pick-up set, so when the faulted section's downstream end is a tie (SEC-1201-04 / TIE-1201-1405) that section is itself the tie's restoration candidate and the tie is closed whenever tie capacity >= the faulted section's load (1490 kW).

# DEF-FLISR-7 evidence package (run rca-backfeed, explore, attempt 2)

Branch `agent/rca-backfeed/explore` @ c43f8c42a2142b0043a5da5bf125e59258866547 (parent a6c2139 from attempt 1). No production code changed.

## Inputs (from recorded human answers)
- Q-EXPLORE-1: FDR-1201 scenario stands in for drill 14 (fault SEC-1201-04, lockout CB-1201, tie TIE-1201-1405).
- Q-EXPLORE-2: function under test is `app.flisr.build_plan`, called from `POST /flisr/plan` (backend/app/api.py:40-49).
- Q-EXPLORE-4: `ruff check backend tools` fails on main in tools/build_coverage_report.py (UP017), an existing exception; touched files linted with `ruff check backend` (clean).

## FDR-1201 topology (backend/data/feeder_model.json)
```
SRC-1201 -[CB-1201 breaker]- BUS-1201 -(SEC-1201-01)- N-1201-1 -[REC-1201-1]- N-1201-1A -(SEC-1201-02)- N-1201-2
 -[SEC-SW-1201-1]- N-1201-2A -(SEC-1201-03)- N-1201-3 -[REC-1201-2]- N-1201-3A -(SEC-1201-04)- N-1201-4 -[TIE-1201-1405 tie, NO]- ALT-1405
```
SEC-1201-04: 341 customers, 1490 kW. Only tie on the feeder is TIE-1201-1405 and it is directly on SEC-1201-04's downstream node N-1201-4.

## Reproduction
1. Load FDR-1201; set fault_indicator True on SEC-1201-01..03, False on SEC-1201-04 (locate_fault -> SEC-1201-04); set CB-1201.open = True (lockout). The shipped model has CB-1201 closed, so the API returns 409 unless lockout is set.
2. `build_plan(feeder, "CB-1201", {"TIE-1201-1405": 2000.0})`, directly and through `POST /flisr/plan` (TestClient, `api.load_network` monkeypatched to return the modified model).
3. Apply the plan's isolation + restoration steps and compute energised nodes from SRC-1201 and ALT-1405.

Command: `pytest backend -q` -> `2 failed, 2 passed`. Both failures are the new DEF-FLISR-7 tests; the 2 existing tests in backend/tests/test_flisr.py still pass.

### Failing test output
```
backend/tests/test_flisr_def_flisr_7.py:22: AssertionError: plan re-energises SEC-1201-04: restoration=[('CB-1201', 'close'), ('TIE-1201-1405', 'close')]
  assert not ({'N-1201-3A', 'N-1201-4'} & {'ALT-1405', 'BUS-1201', 'N-1201-1', 'N-1201-1A', 'N-1201-2', 'N-1201-2A', ...})
backend/tests/test_flisr_def_flisr_7.py:52: AssertionError: POST /flisr/plan closes TIE-1201-1405 onto SEC-1201-04: {... 'restoration': [CB-1201 close, TIE-1201-1405 close 'back-feed 3 nodes from alternate source'], 'customers_restored': 341, 'customers_remaining': 341, 'transferred_load_kw': 1490.0}
```

### Observed vs expected
| | Observed | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| faulted_section | SEC-1201-04 | SEC-1201-04 |
| isolation | REC-1201-2 open (upstream only) | SEC-1201-04 bounded on both ends: REC-1201-2 open and TIE-1201-1405 kept open |
| restoration | CB-1201 close, **TIE-1201-1405 close** | CB-1201 close only (nothing healthy downstream of SEC-1201-04 to restore) |
| SEC-1201-04 after plan | energised from ALT-1405 | de-energised |
| customers_restored / remaining | 341 / 341 (the same 341 customers counted both ways) | 0 / 341 |
| transferred_load_kw | 1490 (the faulted section's own load) | 0 |

## Code excerpts
- flisr.py:41-43 — ties are dropped before isolation is considered:
  `for switch in feeder.switches:` / `if not switch.scada_controllable or switch.kind.value == "tie": continue`
- flisr.py:44-59 — isolation only looks for a switch whose to_node == section.from_node (upstream) or from_node == section.to_node (downstream). For SEC-1201-04 the only downstream match is TIE-1201-1405 (from_node N-1201-4), which was skipped at line 42, so isolation = [REC-1201-2]. No error is raised because `steps` is non-empty (line 60).
- flisr.py:91-122 — every SCADA tie is a restoration candidate; the only gate is `transferred > available` (line 99). Nothing compares candidate_nodes with the faulted section.
- flisr.py:141-151 `_nodes_restored_by` — opens isolated switches, closes the tie, returns `energised_nodes(from tie.from_node) - energised_nodes(from source)`. With REC-1201-2 open, the tie's island is {N-1201-4, N-1201-3A, ALT-1405} = both ends of SEC-1201-04. The faulted section is not subtracted.
- flisr.py:145-146 — the tie is forced closed after the isolated switches are opened, so even a tie listed in isolation would be re-closed in the what-if.
- network.py:90-91 `load_on_nodes` — the 1490 kW "transferred" is SEC-1201-04's own load (to_node N-1201-4 in the candidate set).

## Alternatives ruled out (diagnostic: `PYTHONPATH=backend python backend/tests/rca_def_flisr_7_sweep.py`)
A. FDR-1201, every locatable faulted section x tie capacity:
```
faulted     | cap_kw | isolation                      | restoration                      | tie_candidates                          | back_fed
SEC-1201-02 | 0/1489/1490 | REC-1201-1, SEC-SW-1201-1 | CB close                         | ALT, N-2A, N-3, N-3A, N-4               | False
SEC-1201-02 | 2000   | REC-1201-1, SEC-SW-1201-1      | CB close, TIE close              | ALT, N-2A, N-3, N-3A, N-4               | False
SEC-1201-03 | 0/1489 | REC-1201-2, SEC-SW-1201-1      | CB close                         | ALT, N-3A, N-4                          | False
SEC-1201-03 | 1490/2000 | REC-1201-2, SEC-SW-1201-1   | CB close, TIE close              | ALT, N-3A, N-4                          | False
SEC-1201-04 | 0/1489 | REC-1201-2                     | CB close                         | ALT, N-3A, N-4                          | False
SEC-1201-04 | 1490/2000 | REC-1201-2                  | CB close, TIE close              | ALT, N-3A, N-4                          | True
```
- **Fault mislocation (locate_fault)** — ruled out: faulted_section is SEC-1201-04 as the stand-in scenario specifies; the bad step is the tie close, not the location.
- **Lockout re-close (CB-1201) back-feeds** — ruled out: with tie capacity 0/1489 the plan still closes CB-1201 and SEC-1201-04 stays dead (REC-1201-2 holds it).
- **Capacity check wrong** — ruled out as cause: 1490 vs 1489 is the exact threshold of SEC-1201-04's load, so the check works as written; capacity is the *only* gate, which is the defect.
- **Tie restoration is wrong in general** — ruled out: closing the same tie for faults on SEC-1201-02/03 never back-feeds, because a non-tie switch bounds those sections downstream.
- **Only the tie skip at flisr.py:42** — ruled out as a sufficient explanation (part B counterfactual, monkeypatched in the script, no production edit): adding TIE-1201-1405 to isolation gives isolation [REC-1201-2 open, TIE-1201-1405 open] but restoration still contains TIE-1201-1405 close and back_fed = True, because flisr.py:145-146 re-closes it and lines 91-122 never exclude faulted nodes. Both halves are in the hypothesis.

C. Seeded radial feeders with a tail tie (random.Random(7), 500 cases, 2-8 sections, capacity 0-6000 kW):
```
faulted_adjacent_to_tie | tie_closed | back_fed | cases
False | False | False | 131
False | True  | False | 177
True  | False | False | 42
True  | True  | True  | 150
```
Back-feed happens in exactly the cases where the faulted section's downstream node is the tie and the tie is closed (150/150), and never otherwise (0/350). That fits the hypothesis and nothing broader.

## Falsifiable predictions
1. Any feeder whose faulted section ends at a SCADA tie with capacity >= that section's load gets a plan that closes the tie onto it (sweep C: 150/150).
2. A fault on a section with a non-tie downstream switch is never back-fed by build_plan (sweep A and C: 0/350).
3. Setting the tie capacity below the faulted section's load suppresses the close (sweep A, 1489 kW).
Any counterexample to 1 or 2 refutes the hypothesis.

## Out of scope / for later stages
- Not fixed (explore stage). Fix stage per STD-SAFETY-3/4: both tests above must pass, existing tests unchanged, and a safety invariant over at least 500 seeded inputs (the sweep generator can be reused).
- Blast radius hint for Review: only plans whose faulted section is next to a tie change; the shipped default (fault SEC-1201-03) is unaffected.
- `backend/app/flisr.py` is a protected path (two human reviewers, STD-GOV-6 / STD-SAFETY-1).

root_cause.evaluation:
# DEF-FLISR-7 — Evaluate (run rca-backfeed, attempt 1)

## Prepare
Standards loaded from the brief: STD-GOV v1.1, STD-RCA v1.2, STD-SAFETY v3.1. All three present and readable.
Repo contract: not included in the brief and the brief forbids codebase access, so it was not read. The verdict below does not depend on it (noted, not blocking).

## Verdict: CONFIRMED

Hypothesis under test: `build_plan` never treats a tie switch as a boundary of the faulted section — (a) `_isolation_switches` skips ties (flisr.py:42), and (b) the restoration loop (flisr.py:91-122 via `_nodes_restored_by` flisr.py:136-151) never removes the faulted section's nodes from a tie's pick-up set — so when the faulted section's downstream end is a tie, the tie is closed onto it whenever tie capacity >= that section's load.

### Does the evidence show the mechanism, not just the symptom?
Yes. Three observed numbers in the failing output are only explainable by the faulted section itself being the tie's pick-up set:
- `customers_restored` == `customers_remaining` == 341 (SEC-1201-04's own customer count, counted both as lost and as restored);
- `transferred_load_kw` == 1490.0 == SEC-1201-04's load (network.py:90-91 `load_on_nodes`, to_node N-1201-4 in the candidate set);
- "back-feed 3 nodes" == the island {N-1201-4, N-1201-3A, ALT-1405} = both ends of SEC-1201-04 plus the alternate source, exactly what `_nodes_restored_by` returns with REC-1201-2 open and the tie closed.
The sweep A threshold (1489 kW -> no close, 1490 kW -> close) shows capacity is the only gate and that the gated quantity is the faulted section's load.

### Does it rule out alternatives?
Yes, with data rather than argument:
- Mislocation: faulted_section is SEC-1201-04 in every run.
- CB-1201 reclose as the back-feed path: at 0/1489 kW the plan still closes CB-1201 and SEC-1201-04 stays dead (REC-1201-2 holds it).
- Capacity check defect: 1489/1490 behaves exactly as written.
- Tie restoration wrong in general: the same tie closed for SEC-1201-02/03 faults never back-feeds (sweep A, 0 cases).
- Tie-skip at line 42 alone: the monkeypatched counterfactual (tie added to isolation) still yields TIE close + back_fed=True because flisr.py:145-146 re-closes the tie in the what-if and 91-122 never exclude faulted nodes. This establishes that both halves of the hypothesis are necessary — important for Fix.
- Sweep C (500 seeded feeders): back-feed in 150/150 cases where faulted section ends at the tie and the tie is closed; 0/350 otherwise. A single-cause hypothesis predicts exactly this partition.

### Would the hypothesis predict the failing test's observed value?
Yes. Predicted plan for SEC-1201-04 fault with 2000 kW tie capacity: isolation [REC-1201-2], restoration [CB-1201 close, TIE-1201-1405 close], SEC-1201-04 nodes {N-1201-3A, N-1201-4} energised. That is the recorded assertion failure, both direct and via POST /flisr/plan.

### Falsifiability
Three concrete predictions are stated with the counterexample condition; predictions 1-3 are each exercised by sweep A or C.

## Checks against standards
- STD-RCA-1: single hypothesis, reproduction steps, failing tests (2) with output, observed-vs-expected table, file:line excerpts, alternative-ruling data — all present.
- STD-RCA-2: judged from the package only; no repository used.
- STD-SAFETY-3: defect reproduced by failing tests before any fix; no production code changed in Explore.
- STD-GOV-7: no customer identifiers, personal names or credentials in the package.

## Non-blocking notes for the next stages
1. Code excerpts: only flisr.py:42 is quoted verbatim; lines 44-59, 91-122, 141-151 and network.py:90-91 are paraphrased with file:line. The behavioural evidence (341/341, 1490 kW, 1489/1490 threshold, counterfactual B) independently establishes the mechanism, so this does not weaken the verdict, but Review should spot-check those ranges when it has codebase access.
2. For Fix (STD-SAFETY-4): counterfactual B shows that adding ties to isolation is not sufficient; the restoration candidate set must exclude the faulted section's nodes (or the tie whose from_node/to_node is on the faulted section must be refused). The fail-safe direction is "refuse the tie close", not "best-effort re-route".
3. The "Expected" column's "TIE-1201-1405 kept open" is a fix design choice, not evidence; it was not used in the judgement.
4. `backend/app/flisr.py` is a protected, safety-critical path: two human reviewers (STD-GOV-6, STD-SAFETY-1).
5. Invariant for STD-SAFETY-5 is already stated in the package: "a de-energised fault section is never back-fed during restoration"; the sweep C generator (random.Random(7), 500 cases) can be reused.

# DEF-FLISR-7 — Evaluate (run rca-backfeed, attempt 1)

## Prepare
Standards loaded from the brief: STD-GOV v1.1, STD-RCA v1.2, STD-SAFETY v3.1. All three present and readable.
Repo contract: not included in the brief and the brief forbids codebase access, so it was not read. The verdict below does not depend on it (noted, not blocking).

## Verdict: CONFIRMED

Hypothesis under test: `build_plan` never treats a tie switch as a boundary of the faulted section — (a) `_isolation_switches` skips ties (flisr.py:42), and (b) the restoration loop (flisr.py:91-122 via `_nodes_restored_by` flisr.py:136-151) never removes the faulted section's nodes from a tie's pick-up set — so when the faulted section's downstream end is a tie, the tie is closed onto it whenever tie capacity >= that section's load.

### Does the evidence show the mechanism, not just the symptom?
Yes. Three observed numbers in the failing output are only explainable by the faulted section itself being the tie's pick-up set:
- `customers_restored` == `customers_remaining` == 341 (SEC-1201-04's own customer count, counted both as lost and as restored);
- `transferred_load_kw` == 1490.0 == SEC-1201-04's load (network.py:90-91 `load_on_nodes`, to_node N-1201-4 in the candidate set);
- "back-feed 3 nodes" == the island {N-1201-4, N-1201-3A, ALT-1405} = both ends of SEC-1201-04 plus the alternate source, exactly what `_nodes_restored_by` returns with REC-1201-2 open and the tie closed.
The sweep A threshold (1489 kW -> no close, 1490 kW -> close) shows capacity is the only gate and that the gated quantity is the faulted section's load.

### Does it rule out alternatives?
Yes, with data rather than argument:
- Mislocation: faulted_section is SEC-1201-04 in every run.
- CB-1201 reclose as the back-feed path: at 0/1489 kW the plan still closes CB-1201 and SEC-1201-04 stays dead (REC-1201-2 holds it).
- Capacity check defect: 1489/1490 behaves exactly as written.
- Tie restoration wrong in general: the same tie closed for SEC-1201-02/03 faults never back-feeds (sweep A, 0 cases).
- Tie-skip at line 42 alone: the monkeypatched counterfactual (tie added to isolation) still yields TIE close + back_fed=True because flisr.py:145-146 re-closes the tie in the what-if and 91-122 never exclude faulted nodes. This establishes that both halves of the hypothesis are necessary — important for Fix.
- Sweep C (500 seeded feeders): back-feed in 150/150 cases where faulted section ends at the tie and the tie is closed; 0/350 otherwise. A single-cause hypothesis predicts exactly this partition.

### Would the hypothesis predict the failing test's observed value?
Yes. Predicted plan for SEC-1201-04 fault with 2000 kW tie capacity: isolation [REC-1201-2], restoration [CB-1201 close, TIE-1201-1405 close], SEC-1201-04 nodes {N-1201-3A, N-1201-4} energised. That is the recorded assertion failure, both direct and via POST /flisr/plan.

### Falsifiability
Three concrete predictions are stated with the counterexample condition; predictions 1-3 are each exercised by sweep A or C.

## Checks against standards
- STD-RCA-1: single hypothesis, reproduction steps, failing tests (2) with output, observed-vs-expected table, file:line excerpts, alternative-ruling data — all present.
- STD-RCA-2: judged from the package only; no repository used.
- STD-SAFETY-3: defect reproduced by failing tests before any fix; no production code changed in Explore.
- STD-GOV-7: no customer identifiers, personal names or credentials in the package.

## Non-blocking notes for the next stages
1. Code excerpts: only flisr.py:42 is quoted verbatim; lines 44-59, 91-122, 141-151 and network.py:90-91 are paraphrased with file:line. The behavioural evidence (341/341, 1490 kW, 1489/1490 threshold, counterfactual B) independently establishes the mechanism, so this does not weaken the verdict, but Review should spot-check those ranges when it has codebase access.
2. For Fix (STD-SAFETY-4): counterfactual B shows that adding ties to isolation is not sufficient; the restoration candidate set must exclude the faulted section's nodes (or the tie whose from_node/to_node is on the faulted section must be refused). The fail-safe direction is "refuse the tie close", not "best-effort re-route".
3. The "Expected" column's "TIE-1201-1405 kept open" is a fix design choice, not evidence; it was not used in the judgement.
4. `backend/app/flisr.py` is a protected, safety-critical path: two human reviewers (STD-GOV-6, STD-SAFETY-1).
5. Invariant for STD-SAFETY-5 is already stated in the package: "a de-energised fault section is never back-fed during restoration"; the sweep C generator (random.Random(7), 500 cases) can be reused.

# DEF-FLISR-7 — Explore evidence package (run rca-backfeed, round 1)

**Status: BLOCKED.** The required input (the drill-14 savecase in `backend/tests/data`) does not exist. The defect *class* reproduces on the shipped network model. Whether that is the same failure seen in drill 14 has not been shown (see questions).

## Hypothesis (one, falsifiable)
`build_plan` (backend/app/flisr.py:65) back-feeds the faulted section whenever that section's downstream boundary is a tie switch. Two things combine to cause it. First, `_isolation_switches` never opens a tie (`switch.kind.value == "tie"` → `continue`, flisr.py:42). Second, the restoration loop (flisr.py:91-122) picks nodes through `_nodes_restored_by` (flisr.py:136-151), which only subtracts nodes still fed from the feeder's own source and never subtracts the faulted section. So the tie's "restored" node set contains the faulted section, and a `close` on that tie is emitted.
**Prediction:** a back-feed happens if and only if the located faulted section is the one next to a tie. It never happens for any other faulted section, and location is not at fault.

## Reproduction
1. `pip install -e './backend[dev]'` (already installed).
2. Shipped model `backend/data/feeder_model.json`, feeder FDR-1201: radial CB-1201 → SEC-01 → REC-1201-1 → SEC-02 → SEC-SW-1201-1 → SEC-03 → REC-1201-2 → SEC-04 (N-1201-3A→N-1201-4) → TIE-1201-1405 (normally open) → ALT-1405.
3. Set fault indicators on SEC-1201-01..03 (fault beyond them = SEC-1201-04), lockout CB-1201 open, tie capacity 2000 kW.
4. `pytest backend/tests/test_flisr_def_flisr_7.py -q` (branch `agent/rca-backfeed/explore`, commit a6c2139).

## Failing test output
```
E       AssertionError: plan re-energises SEC-1201-04: restoration=[('CB-1201', 'close'), ('TIE-1201-1405', 'close')]
E       assert not ({'N-1201-3A', 'N-1201-4'} & {'ALT-1405', 'BUS-1201', 'N-1201-1', 'N-1201-1A', 'N-1201-2', 'N-1201-2A', ...})
backend/tests/test_flisr_def_flisr_7.py:22: AssertionError
1 failed, 2 passed   (full suite: existing 2 tests still pass)
```

## Observed vs expected
| | Expected | Observed (`build_plan` output) |
|---|---|---|
| faulted_section | SEC-1201-04 | SEC-1201-04 (correct) |
| isolation | REC-1201-2 open **and** TIE-1201-1405 held open | only REC-1201-2 open |
| restoration | CB-1201 close only; tie not closed | CB-1201 close, **TIE-1201-1405 close** ("back-feed 3 nodes from alternate source") |
| customers | restored 0 from tie, remaining 341 | restored 341 **and** remaining 341 (faulted customers counted as restored too) |
| transferred_load_kw | 0 | 1490 (the faulted section's own load) |

## Code excerpts
- flisr.py:41-43 — isolation skips ties:
  `for switch in feeder.switches: if not switch.scada_controllable or switch.kind.value == "tie": continue`
- flisr.py:85-86 — `plan.isolation = _isolation_switches(...)`; `isolated_mrids = {...}`
- flisr.py:91-96 — restoration iterates every SCADA tie; `candidate_nodes = _nodes_restored_by(feeder, switch.mrid, isolated_mrids)`. There is no check against the faulted section, and no check of whether the tie itself is an isolation point.
- flisr.py:142-146 — in the working copy, `if switch.mrid in isolated_switches: switch.open = True` and then `if switch.mrid == tie_mrid: switch.open = False`. The second line overrides the first, so a tie listed as an isolation point is still closed.
- flisr.py:148-151 — `return from_tie - from_source`. Only nodes fed from the own source are removed. The faulted section's nodes (N-1201-3A, N-1201-4) are cut off from the source by REC-1201-2, so they stay in the set.
- Entry point: api.py:40-45 `POST /flisr/plan` → `flisr.build_plan`. No function named `plan_restoration` exists.

## Alternatives ruled out (seeded sweep `~/rca/sweep.py`, `random.Random(7)`, 600 radial feeders of 2-7 sections, tie at the tail, fault on a random section)
| Alternative | Data | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Wrong fault location (`locate_fault`) | located correctly 447/447 cases with indications (153 had no indication → manual patrol, no plan) | ruled out |
| General restoration bug (any fault gets back-fed) | not adjacent to the tie: 0/279 back-fed | ruled out |
| Tie capacity / transfer check | capacity set to 1e9 in the sweep and 2000 kW (> 1490 kW) in the repro; the check is about load, not topology | not a factor |
| Fixing isolation alone (removing the tie skip at :42) | runtime monkeypatch B: still 168/168 back-fed; the plan becomes self-contradictory: isolation `TIE open`, restoration `TIE close` (because of :145 overriding :143) | ruled out as sole cause; both :42 and :91-151 are involved |
| Both parts together | monkeypatch C (ties opened for isolation **and** a tie that is an isolation point is never a restoration candidate): 0/168 back-fed, 0/279 non-adjacent changed | consistent with the hypothesis |
| Prediction "iff adjacent to the tie" | adjacent: 168/168 back-fed; not adjacent: 0/279 | holds on 447/447 |

The monkeypatches were runtime-only experiments (`~/rca/counterfactual.py`). No production code was changed.

## Not established
- That drill 14 is this scenario. The savecase is missing, so drill 14's topology, indicators and tie are unknown. A different drill-14 cause (e.g. a meshed or branched topology, a non-SCADA boundary switch, or wrong indications) cannot be excluded.

## Findings for the assessor
- STD-SAFETY-7 tool classification: pytest plus the seeded sweep are a T2 tool under IEC 61508-3 (verification tools whose errors could fail to reveal a defect but cannot inject one into the executable). No certification credit is claimed.
- Baseline `ruff check backend tools` fails on `main` with an existing UP017 in tools/build_coverage_report.py:183, which this stage did not touch. `ruff check backend/tests` passes on the new test.
- Repo contract mismatch: the layer map lists `backend/app/state_estimation.py` and `backend/app/main.py`, but the actual files are `state_estimator.py` and `api.py`.


SEC-1201-04: 341 customers, 1490 kW. Only tie on the feeder is TIE-1201-1405 and it is directly on SEC-1201-04's downstream node N-1201-4.

2. `build_plan(feeder, "CB-1201", {"TIE-1201-1405": 2000.0})`, directly and through `POST /flisr/plan` (TestClient, `api.load_network` monkeypatched to return the modified model).
3. Apply the plan's isolation + restoration steps and compute energised nodes from SRC-1201 and ALT-1405.

## Code excerpts
- flisr.py:41-43 — ties are dropped before isolation is considered:
  `for switch in feeder.switches:` / `if not switch.scada_controllable or switch.kind.value == "tie": continue`
- flisr.py:44-59 — isolation only looks for a switch whose to_node == section.from_node (upstream) or from_node == section.to_node (downstream). For SEC-1201-04 the only downstream match is TIE-1201-1405 (from_node N-1201-4), which was skipped at line 42, so isolation = [REC-1201-2]. No error is raised because `steps` is non-empty (line 60).
- flisr.py:91-122 — every SCADA tie is a restoration candidate; the only gate is `transferred > available` (line 99). Nothing compares candidate_nodes with the faulted section.
- flisr.py:141-151 `_nodes_restored_by` — opens isolated switches, closes the tie, returns `energised_nodes(from tie.from_node) - energised_nodes(from source)`. With REC-1201-2 open, the tie's island is {N-1201-4, N-1201-3A, ALT-1405} = both ends of SEC-1201-04. The faulted section is not subtracted.
- flisr.py:145-146 — the tie is forced closed after the isolated switches are opened, so even a tie listed in isolation would be re-closed in the what-if.
- network.py:90-91 `load_on_nodes` — the 1490 kW "transferred" is SEC-1201-04's own load (to_node N-1201-4 in the candidate set).

## Alternatives ruled out (diagnostic: `PYTHONPATH=backend python backend/tests/rca_def_flisr_7_sweep.py`)
A. FDR-1201, every locatable faulted section x tie capacity:
```
faulted     | cap_kw | isolation                      | restoration                      | tie_candidates                          | back_fed
SEC-1201-02 | 0/1489/1490 | REC-1201-1, SEC-SW-1201-1 | CB close                         | ALT, N-2A, N-3, N-3A, N-4               | False
SEC-1201-02 | 2000   | REC-1201-1, SEC-SW-1201-1      | CB close, TIE close              | ALT, N-2A, N-3, N-3A, N-4               | False
SEC-1201-03 | 0/1489 | REC-1201-2, SEC-SW-1201-1      | CB close                         | ALT, N-3A, N-4                          | False
SEC-1201-03 | 1490/2000 | REC-1201-2, SEC-SW-1201-1   | CB close, TIE close              | ALT, N-3A, N-4                          | False
SEC-1201-04 | 0/1489 | REC-1201-2                     | CB close                         | ALT, N-3A, N-4                          | False
SEC-1201-04 | 1490/2000 | REC-1201-2                  | CB close, TIE close              | ALT, N-3A, N-4                          | True
```
- **Fault mislocation (locate_fault)** — ruled out: faulted_section is SEC-1201-04 as the stand-in scenario specifies; the bad step is the tie close, not the location.
- **Lockout re-close (CB-1201) back-feeds** — ruled out: with tie capacity 0/1489 the plan still closes CB-1201 and SEC-1201-04 stays dead (REC-1201-2 holds it).
- **Capacity check wrong** — ruled out as cause: 1490 vs 1489 is the exact threshold of SEC-1201-04's load, so the check works as written; capacity is the *only* gate, which is the defect.
- **Tie restoration is wrong in general** — ruled out: closing the same tie for faults on SEC-1201-02/03 never back-feeds, because a non-tie switch bounds those sections downstream.
- **Only the tie skip at flisr.py:42** — ruled out as a sufficient explanation (part B counterfactual, monkeypatched in the script, no production edit): adding TIE-1201-1405 to isolation gives isolation [REC-1201-2 open, TIE-1201-1405 open] but restoration still contains TIE-1201-1405 close and back_fed = True, because flisr.py:145-146 re-closes it and lines 91-122 never exclude faulted nodes. Both halves are in the hypothesis.

C. Seeded radial feeders with a tail tie (random.Random(7), 500 cases, 2-8 sections, capacity 0-6000 kW):
```
faulted_adjacent_to_tie | tie_closed | back_fed | cases
False | False | False | 131
False | True  | False | 177
True  | False | False | 42
True  | True  | True  | 150
```
Back-feed happens in exactly the cases where the faulted section's downstream node is the tie and the tie is closed (150/150), and never otherwise (0/350). That fits the hypothesis and nothing broader.

## Falsifiable predictions
1. Any feeder whose faulted section ends at a SCADA tie with capacity >= that section's load gets a plan that closes the tie onto it (sweep C: 150/150).
2. A fault on a section with a non-tie downstream switch is never back-fed by build_plan (sweep A and C: 0/350).
3. Setting the tie capacity below the faulted section's load suppresses the close (sweep A, 1489 kW).
Any counterexample to 1 or 2 refutes the hypothesis.
